provenance.binary_encoder: reference/engine/cdx_exchange.py plus generator-local published scheme/step/bracket tags and native-observed arrow 0x8021
provenance.native_arrow_tag_evidence: ChemDraw 26 native captures and crates/io/src/exchange/mod.rs; 2026-11-17 native spot-check of case 007: CDXML blue arrow present, reference 0x8027 CDX arrow absent. Generator therefore writes 0x8021. Inputs remain synthetic, not native-authored.

format_notes: CDXML/CDX and files.cds (.drawing.cds) are full drawing inputs. files.style_cds and its variants are separate empty-artwork style controls.
CDS uses CDX framing with packed document LabelStyle 0x080a and CaptionStyle 0x080b. Full stationery preserves all source artwork; separate style controls contain an empty page.
CDX normally has the ChemDraw-compatible 22-byte header; one case uses the published 28-byte header. Compact stationery additionally has padded and rootless legacy CDS variants.

The published SDK and Python reference use arrow object 0x8027; native ChemDraw 26 uses 0x8021. Native case 007 spot-check on 2026-11-17 showed 0x8027 silently losing the arrow, so this generator locally substitutes 0x8021 without using ReShiki's exporter.
Font table IDs use their own namespace in the format, but this generator also keeps them disjoint from all drawing object IDs.
Counts are assertions about visible/imported model objects, not source XML element counts. Image graphics are included in graphics; atom label text is excluded from annotations.
Source semantic expectations are handwritten generator rules, not learned from ReShiki output. Unsupported and malformed cases require transactional rejection.
Curves may import as editable paths and curve-only groups can combine paths. Parametric source shape identity and exact exported graphic counts are not promised.
The retained Python codec cannot encode arbitrary alpha properties. Such missing binary variants are explicit in each case, never silently stripped.
